title: Cesium-137 and Strontium-90 Decay
learningObjectives: Explain that a half-life is the time for half of a radioactive sample to decay
Compare 30-year half-lives of fission products with the much longer half-life of plutonium-239

explanations.text: Fission products such as cesium-137 and strontium-90 lose half their radioactivity about every 30 years, following exponential decay.

evidence.quote: Strontium-90 and cesium-137 have half-lives of about 30 years (half the radioactivity will decay in 30 years).

explanations.text: Radioactive isotopes do not disappear instantly; they decay over time toward stable, harmless materials at rates set by their half-lives.

evidence.quote: Radioactive isotopes eventually decay, or disintegrate, to harmless materials.

explanations.text: Some heavier elements decay far more slowly than fission products, remaining hazardous for thousands of years.

evidence.quote: Plutonium-239 has a half-life of 24,000 years.

predictions.prompt: A 100 gram cesium-137 sample with a 30-year half-life is stored for 30 years. How much remains?
A 200 gram cesium-137 sample with the same 30-year half-life stored for 60 years.
An 80 gram sample with a 20-year half-life stored for 40 years.
